scenes.title: A Promise Made: Will You Keep It?

elements.content:
A Promise Made:

Will You Keep It?
Maya lends her book
Leo makes a promise
Next day: book returned

Observe

What happens when you keep your promise?

Wonder

Would your friend trust you again? Why?

actions.text: Hello everyone, and welcome to our class! I'm glad you're here. Today we begin something very close to our everyday lives — promises. Take a look at our title: A Promise Made — Will You Keep It? Over the next few pages, we will learn what a promise really is, why trust matters, and how to keep our word.
Let's start with a story — a real one, like something that could happen at your school. Maya has a favourite book. She loves it very much. One day, she lends it to her friend Leo.

Leo takes the book and makes a clear promise. He says, 'I will return it tomorrow after school.' Maya hesitates for a moment — then she chooses to trust him and hands over the book. Did you notice? Maya gives her trust before Leo proves anything. Trust is something we give first, and it can grow or shrink later.

Now cut to the next morning. Leo remembers the promise. He packs the book in his bag, and he gives it back exactly when he said he would — the next day, after school. Maya smiles. She is relieved and happy, because her friend kept his word.

Before I explain anything, let's just observe. What happens when you keep your promise? Something quietly changes between two people — a warm feeling, a little more safety. Can you picture that feeling between Maya and Leo?

And here is something to wonder about: would your friend be more likely to trust you again? Why do you think that is? Hold that idea in your mind — this is exactly what we will explore together today. Words like promise, commitment, and trust may sound big, but they are simply about what we say and what we do next.

actions.topic: Would your friend be more likely to trust you again? Why?
actions.prompt: Think of a time a friend of yours kept a promise — or did not keep one. How did you feel, and how did it change the way you trusted them the next time?

scenes.title: The Emotional Bank Account: How Does Trust Grow?

actions.text: We just talked about promises, commitments, and trust — about what we say and what we do next. Now here is a picture to help us think about trust. Imagine two friends share an invisible Emotional Bank Account. Every kind, honest action is like putting something in. Every broken promise takes something out. Let's explore it together.

actions.content: The account jar with its soft light, and the two friends whose closeness changes.

actions.text: Before we test anything, make a prediction. If someone always keeps their promises and really listens to you, how would you feel about trusting them? Take a quiet moment and hold your answer.

actions.content: Promises kept, again and again.

actions.text: Look at what happens. Keeping a promise is a deposit — and when it happens again and again, the light grows brighter and the two friends move closer. Did your prediction match what you see?
Now predict the opposite. What might happen if someone keeps saying they will do something, but never follows through? Watch closely.

actions.content: The same promise, broken again and again.
Notice how one broken promise dims the light — and a repeated one dims it much more.

actions.text: So here is the big discovery. This account is only a picture to help us understand trust. It is not a real bank account, and it is not a score we can count. Trust grows through consistent actions, not just words. On the next page, we will think about how to make promises we can actually keep.

scenes.title: Make Promises You Can Actually Keep

actions.text: A moment ago we saw that trust grows through steady actions, not big words. So how do we make a promise we can actually keep? Let's build a promise ourselves and test it. Here is our promise builder. Four dials: how big the promise is, how clear the words are, whether you can really do it, and when it will happen. Let's start with a promise that sounds impressive. I will finish all my homework, clean my room, help everyone, and never forget anything!

actions.content: Situation A: a huge, vague promise with no clear time.
Press play to run one whole week with this promise.

actions.text: Watch the week unfold. Take a quiet moment — what do you notice? The promise is so big and so fuzzy that the character does not even know where to start. Look at the overwhelm meter climbing, and the promise bank staying low. Nothing actually gets done. So here is my question for you: which promise is more realistic and easier to follow through on — this one, or a small, clear one?

actions.content: Situation B: 'I will put my school bag near the door tonight.' Press play again.

actions.text: Now look at this promise instead. One small thing. Very clear words. Something the character really can do. And a time: tonight. Press play once more and compare the two runs. Amazing — the week finishes calmly, and the promise is kept. The promise did not need to sound impressive. It needed to be possible. So what made the difference? Let's uncover the three checks that turn a wish into a promise you can truly keep.

actions.content: The three checks: Is it specific? Can I realistically do it? When will I do it?

actions.text: Here they are. Is it specific — do I know exactly what I am promising? Can I realistically do it — is it something I truly can manage? And when will I do it — is there a clear time? Before you make your next promise, ask yourself three questions: Can I do it? When will I do it? What might get in the way? A promise you can genuinely keep is worth far more than one that only sounds big.

scenes.title: What If You Cannot Keep a Promise?

actions.text: We just covered how to make promises we can keep, but what happens when life throws a curveball? Today, we're going to see what happens when a promise gets tough to keep.
Meet Leo. He promised to return a book today, but he realizes he just can't finish reading it in time. We need to help him keep the friendship bond strong.

actions.content: Press start to see how the situation unfolds.
Begin the puzzle with the starting scenario.

actions.text: You have a set of moves—some responsible and some avoidant. Your job is to drag these moves onto the timeline. But more than just placing them, you have to decide *when* to place them.

actions.content: Pay attention to the gaps of time between the timeline slots.

actions.text: Think about the choices Leo has. If he hides the problem or waits until the deadline passes, how might that affect the trust in his friendship?

state.feedback: Avoidance has caused the bond to drop significantly.

actions.content: Demonstrate the consequence of waiting too long.

actions.text: Now, let's try the responsible path. When should Leo speak up? Where is the best moment to address a problem before it grows into a big mistake?

actions.content: Select the move: 'Speak up early and apologize.'

state.feedback: Communicating honestly early has protected the friendship.

actions.content: Place the key move early to show positive impact.
Reveal the core lesson on rebuilding trust after the puzzle.

scenes.title: Your Promise, Your Plan: Put Trust into Action

actions.text: On the last page we looked at what to do when a promise cannot be kept. Now let's put it all together and build your very own promise tracker, step by step.

actions.content: Start here: your promise. It can be to yourself, or to a family member or friend.

actions.text: Every promise needs a plan. Let's look at two important steps: the action you will take, and the real time you will do it.

actions.content: A promise with a real time is much easier to keep than a promise with no time at all.
Keep it simple — tick a box or colour a star, and watch your promise grow day by day.
Your accountability partner checks in with kind questions — they encourage you, they never judge.
And here is the finish line: trust grows when our actions match our words.

actions.text: So remember the key sequence: PROMISE, then PLAN, then FOLLOW THROUGH, then COMMUNICATE. Here is your closing takeaway — trust is built when our actions match our words. Make promises that matter, keep them when you can, and speak honestly when plans change. This week, choose one small promise, write your plan, and start. That is how trust grows, one kept promise at a time.
